unit.title: Communities and Maps Around the World

lesson.title: Land and Water on a Map
lesson.subject: social-studies

contentBlocks.text: You can read map symbols now. Today: use a real world map to find the two biggest things it shows — land and water!

On most maps, land is shown in green or brown, and water — oceans, seas, lakes, rivers — is shown in blue. Looking at a real world map, most of the blue you see is ocean, the huge bodies of water that separate the large landmasses called continents. Look at a world map (or the picture on your worksheet) and point out one area of land and one area of water.
You just used real map-reading skills to identify land and water on a world map! Tomorrow we'll review everything from this week.

objectives: Identify land and water on a map using color (green/brown for land, blue for water)
Point out a real example of land and water on a world map
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review map symbols from yesterday.
2. Introduce land (green/brown) vs. water (blue) coloring on a world map.
3. Look at a real world map or globe together, pointing out land and water.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Close by finding the ocean or landmass closest to where the child lives.
differentiationTips: Struggling: use a globe or large world map poster rather than a small printed image, for easier visual scanning
Ready for more: ask the child to count how many separate large landmasses (continents) they can identify on the map
A real map or globe is genuinely important here — this lesson is much weaker without one
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a map-reading activity — check that the child can correctly point to an area of land and an area of water on a real map, using color as the guide.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the course's 'introduction to reading maps' description, applying color-based map reading to the largest, most fundamental map feature: land versus water.
